authority.rule: When documentation conflicts with current source/runtime behavior, current source wins.

aiCli.purpose: Low-token desktop tool surface for coding agents; reuses Stable Runtime services and Execution evidence.

runtimeRules: For coding-agent desktop interaction, inspect `opendesk ai schema` and `opendesk ai capabilities`; prefer its window metadata, targeted screenshots, deterministic primitives, and reusable recipes before full-screen visual reasoning.
Prefer stable documented APIs for new scripts.
Prefer page.ensurePermissions for permission-gated desktop workflows.
Prefer Vision.runOCR or Vision.detectUI for structured OCR/UI text work; use OCR.extractText for simple local text extraction.
Use ImageColor as a secondary pixel/template/color primitive, not as a replacement for semantic verification.
Prefer axios for normal script HTTP requests; axios is a polyfill backed by http.request.

NativeExtensions is an Experimental manifest-discovered immutable binding. Normal local CLI calls use NativeExtensions.<namespace>.<method>(businessParams) with routes fixed by the Host; it discovers only the program-relative bundle directory by default. HTTP and MCP cannot enable or call it. The low-level NativeExtension.call compatibility surface requires the separate -experimental-unsafe-native-extension-call local diagnostic gate.
The ui global is always present but dormant by default. Enable it with -ui or strict clawdesk.runtime.json; HTML/CSS declares the view and all business API calls stay in the JavaScript controller.

Dialog is always present but fail-closed without the ui capability. Its alert, confirm, and prompt methods are asynchronous native modal dialogs; global alert/confirm/prompt are thin polyfill aliases, never browser-style blocking calls.
Treat upgraded/playwright surfaces as compatibility facades, not a complete Playwright browser engine.
Do not use retired TestMonkey documentation as a current API authority.

globals.name: page
globals.summary: Desktop page entry: screenshot, open URL/App, waits and permissions.

globals.name: Events
globals.source: native runtime wrapper + explicit polling backend
globals.notes: Polling is reported in capability and event payloads; no MCP/HTTP surface and no GlobalShortcut duplication. Window events are unsupported on platforms where the existing window facade is unavailable.

globals.name: App
globals.source: native Runtime wrapper + existing NSWorkspace/process/window backends
globals.identity: PID, name, bundleId, or path; stable bundle/path identity is preferred and one identity may group multiple process instances
globals.readiness: process or an existing Window-facade row owned by a matching PID; custom predicates are explicitly unsupported
globals.lifecycle: Promise workers are execution-scoped, context-cancelable, timeout-bounded, and joined during Runtime teardown
globals.compatibility: page.openApp and AI CLI app.open retain their public contract while sharing the same launch bridge; System process and Window APIs remain independent
globals.platformBehavior: macOS+cgo uses NSWorkspace/Open/NSRunningApplication and is fixture-verified; Windows/Linux use explicit partial process fallbacks and are not live verified
globals.surface: JavaScript Runtime only in this phase; no HTTP or MCP method was added

globals.name: Notifications
globals.source: execution-owned Runtime wrapper + macOS UserNotifications own-app model
globals.scope: macOS lists and removes only notifications delivered by the OpenDesk app identity; arbitrary application notifications are not exposed
globals.privacy: title and message are redacted by default and require includeContent=true; metadata stays scoped to OpenDesk
globals.identity: opaque UserNotifications request identifier plus OpenDesk app identity and delivery timestamp; duplicate content is not treated as identity
globals.lifecycle: waitFor uses a bounded own-app poll, prefers new notifications by default, runs under the execution context, and is canceled and joined during teardown
globals.unsupported: activate is not exposed because public UserNotifications APIs report user actions but cannot simulate them; Events does not claim notification.changed
globals.platformBehavior: Windows UserNotificationListener requires manifest capability, package/app identity, and user consent not present in the current OpenDesk host; Linux has no equivalent stable unified backend. Both fail closed.
globals.surface: JavaScript Runtime only; outbound sending remains the existing notify() global

globals.name: window
globals.source: native facade + CoreGraphics/System Events or Win32 backend + normalization polyfill
globals.identity: Every observed row has an id. A uniquely resolved row uses platform:pid:native:nativeHandle; metadata-poor or cross-Space rows use platform:pid:unresolved and must not be treated as stable. Title actions resolve a unique current title first and reject duplicate titles.
globals.coordinateSpace: macOS uses global display points with a primary-display top-left origin and possible negative secondary coordinates; Windows uses virtual-screen logical coordinates subject to DPI awareness.
globals.staleTarget: A title action that resolves successfully but loses or renames its target before the backend action reports STALE_TARGET. Initial absence reports NOT_FOUND.
globals.platformBehavior: macOS core paths are live fixture-verified but arbitrary actions remain permission/app/Space dependent; Windows source is target-compiled but not live verified in this macOS evidence run; Linux is explicit Unsupported.
globals.surface: The existing JavaScript window facade was extended; no second backend, HTTP route, MCP tool, Accessibility tree, or Spaces manager was added.

globals.name: Screen
globals.notes: Display inventory, pixel, and screenshot methods remain stable. Existing Screen owns display inventory; no duplicate Display global was added. macOS CoreGraphics mode read/list are available and setDisplayMode is Experimental with synchronous readback and caller restore. Brightness is explicitly Unsupported and delegated to hardware-specific Native Extensions. selectRegion/startRecording are Experimental on macOS; audio and frame streaming are explicitly unavailable.

globals.name: System
globals.status: stable reads with experimental session actions
globals.sessionSafety: lock, logout, and startScreenSaver require confirm=true before backend access; success returns initiated=true and verified=false because request acceptance is not a postcondition
globals.sessionIdentity: getSessionState returns only normalized user/session identity and state; unavailable booleans including locked are null rather than inferred
globals.platformBehavior: macOS public CGSessionCopyCurrentDictionary supports read-only WindowServer session state and leaves locked unknown; ScreenSaverEngine launch is Experimental while lock/logout are unsupported. Windows uses public LockWorkStation/ExitWindowsEx candidates but remains target-runtime unverified. Linux requires loginctl plus XDG_SESSION_ID and remains target-runtime unverified.
globals.compatibility: existing shutdown, restart, and sleep remain the separate legacy power-control surface; this task does not create a second System or Power namespace

globals.name: clipboard
globals.capability: Stable text compatibility API on all supported desktops; experimental rich text, PNG, and file representations currently use NSPasteboard on macOS. clipboard.write verifies every requested representation, clipboard.read returns a changeCount-consistent snapshot, and formats:[] reads metadata only. Binary values are canonical base64, files are absolute paths, and Events clipboard.changed reports metadata only.

globals.name: NativeExtensions
globals.source: strict manifest registry plus host-generated immutable binding
globals.condition: available to local CLI JavaScript by default after a complete source-free bundle is installed beside the actual executable; the -script path does not affect discovery; HTTP, MCP, and other remote execution transports never inject, enable, redirect, or call it
globals.summary: Discovers strict extension.json bundles from exactly one portable/app-bundled program-relative root; it does not compile or install source examples, generates frozen namespaces and method closures, and starts one validated executable only when a generated method is called.
globals.platformStatus: V1 has Darwin/Linux/Windows implementation candidates; macOS-only examples or Runtime Evidence do not mean the whole API is macOS-only. go-basic is target-buildable Go; macos-vision is macOS-only. A target without target-machine Runtime Evidence is Not Evaluated, not Unsupported.
globals.migration: legacy prototype roots are not scanned or auto-moved/copied/merged/deleted
globals.lifecycle: registry frozen per execution; start a new execution after install or upgrade; no hot reload
globals.errorModel: method failure throws NativeExtensionsError; successful calls return the extension result directly
doesNotExecute: third-party JavaScript facade files during discovery

globals.name: notify
globals.signature: notify(message: string): void; notify(options: OpenDeskNotifyOptions): void
globals.timeout: accepted for compatibility but ignored by current platform notification backends
globals.result: undefined on backend submission success; throws on invalid input or backend failure
globals.validation: options fields use their documented primitive types; timeout must be finite; title and message must be valid UTF-8 without NUL
globals.macOSBackend: native UserNotifications with OpenDesk.app identity; plain CLI and Scheduler re-enter the sibling OpenDesk.app notification-only helper and never use ScriptEditor2/osascript; missing app identity, denied alerts, timeout, helper stderr/exit, and request submission failures throw
globals.sound: sound=true requests the platform default sound; actual sound remains subject to macOS and user settings
globals.visibility: success means NotificationCenter accepted the request after authorization checks; Focus/Do Not Disturb, display sharing/mirroring, and other OS policy may still suppress user-visible presentation

globals.name: Dialog
globals.source: host-owned native binding plus thin polyfill aliases
globals.condition: always injected but DIALOG_DISABLED without the ui capability; CLI needs -ui or trusted config, HTTP additionally needs server enablement, per-request ui and loopback source; Scheduler and MCP have no Dialog opt-in
globals.platformBehavior: macOS normal AppKit top-level window through the existing Custom UI native host; unsupported platforms reject DIALOG_UNSUPPORTED_PLATFORM
globals.asyncControlFlow: Promise-only: no onConfirm/onCancel options callbacks and no synchronous EventLoop blocking. await pauses only its async flow; then/catch/finally run on the owner EventLoop. An unobserved Dialog Promise is closed during execution teardown rather than retaining the execution indefinitely; all competing terminal paths settle exactly once.
globals.promptResult: prompt resolves a string on confirm and null on user cancellation. Public examples display a non-sensitive result in a following Dialog.alert; secure or otherwise sensitive input must not be echoed to logs, notifications, or another Dialog.
globals.privacy: secure prompt uses a password input; Dialog never writes message, defaultValue, or prompt input to ordinary logs, errors, summaries, events, or HTTP responses

globals.name: Audio
globals.source: native runtime wrapper + macOS CoreAudio HAL
globals.capture: not implemented; microphone and systemAudio are explicitly false in capability discovery
globals.soundCompatibility: Sound keeps blocking MP3/WAV compatibility methods and adds execution-scoped controllable playback sessions
globals.platformBehavior: darwin+cgo uses CoreAudio; non-CGO macOS and other platforms report unavailable and reject instead of silent no-op

globals.name: ui
globals.source: native process driver plus EventLoop bridge
globals.condition: always present but dormant by default; local CLI or strict project config authorization is required, while HTTP additionally requires server opt-in, per-request capability declaration, and a loopback peer
globals.platformBehavior: macOS AppKit/WebKit host; Windows and Linux report available=false and createWindow rejects UNSUPPORTED_PLATFORM

globals.name: FloatingWindow
globals.source: Button-first facade over the Custom UI driver
globals.condition: injected only when Custom UI is explicitly authorized; constructible instances accept orientation horizontal (default, 1-32 ordered buttons with toolbar.maxWidth 60-960pt, maxColumns 1-19 and optional maxRows 1-32 automatic-wrap constraints) or vertical (1-5 ordered buttons in one native column; no toolbar wrapping constraints), 150 reviewed built-in SF Symbols, synchronous or Promise callbacks, post-show state updates, button-level single-flight, and structured callback errors; invalid layout constraints, unknown orientation and overflow are INVALID_SPEC

globals.name: Global APIs
globals.summary: 无需 import 即可直接调用的计时器、等待、console 日志、剪贴板快捷函数、取消控制、通知与 URL 参数接口。
